title: peek_requests.moderation_status defaults to 'pending' while the live contract requires 'approved', so any insert path omitting it strands the request invisibly

impact: A Peek Request created by any path that does not explicitly set moderation_status is invisible to the public thread and cannot be accepted by the seller — it strands with no error surfaced to the buyer. The safe default is the one the MVP contract requires, not the legacy moderation default.

title: MFA is enforced only in the browser; no assurance-level check exists in any policy, function or trigger, so an aal1 token reaches every admin RPC directly
location: src/App.jsx:115-132,147-151; src/services/authService.js:159-165; supabase/migrations (all 159 — zero matches for aal1/aal2/assurance/amr); supabase/migrations/0088_private_authorization_helper_implementations.sql
evidence: useMfaGate calls authService.mfaChallengeRequired(), which reads currentLevel/nextLevel client-side and returns a boolean used only to choose which React component to render. Grepping all migrations for aal1, aal2, assurance and amr returns no matches. private.is_admin() tests role membership only. Supabase exposes the level in SQL as auth.jwt() ->> 'aal', so the control is available and unused.
impact: MFA provides no protection against API access, which is the threat it is deployed for. An attacker who compromises an admin password signs in, receives a valid aal1 session, is shown the MFA challenge screen, and simply does not use the SPA — calling PostgREST and the admin RPCs directly with the aal1 bearer token. Every server-side check passes because none require aal2. Admin capability covers user suspension and ban, listing and service takedown, Peek removal, conversation action and verified-business decisions.
reproduction: Sign in as an MFA-enrolled admin, stop at the challenge screen, take the access token from the session and call an admin RPC directly against /rest/v1/rpc/ — it succeeds
root_cause: MFA added as a client-side route gate without a corresponding database-side assurance-level predicate
recommended_fix: Require auth.jwt() ->> 'aal' = 'aal2' inside private.is_admin() and private.is_super_admin() for accounts holding a verified factor, or add an aal2 predicate to admin RLS policies and the prelude of every admin RPC
test_to_prove_fix: pgTAP asserting an admin RPC called with an aal1 JWT is denied while the same call with aal2 succeeds
notes: Appendix C gate 'MFA cannot be route-bypassed' = FAIL. Precondition is prior credential compromise, which is why this is rated P1 rather than P0; treat as P0 if MFA is the compensating control for admin password compromise.

title: Search mixes keyset cursor pagination with an offset range() path

impact: Offset pagination is unstable under concurrent inserts: a listing published while a buyer pages can push results down so an item is shown twice or skipped entirely. Inconsistent with the cursor strategy used elsewhere.

root_cause: Two pagination strategies introduced at different times and not reconciled
recommended_fix: Move the remaining offset path onto the cursor RPC
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting no duplicate or skipped row across a page boundary when a row is inserted mid-scan
notes: Primary search path already uses the correct strategy

title: Sellers cannot mark a listing sold; the only terminal action is unavailable
evidence: owner_transition_listing restricts p_action to ('submit','pause','resume','unavailable'). The listing_status enum contains 'sold', 'rented' and 'under_offer', but no migration or client path writes them: grepping for set status/next_status to 'sold' returns nothing.
impact: A marketplace cannot record the outcome that matters most. Sold and withdrawn collapse into one state, so buyers lose the signal that an asset actually transacted, sellers cannot close a listing honestly, and the product loses its only free measure of whether it is working. For property and vehicles, a stale live listing that was actually sold is also a direct trust problem.
reproduction: Open /my-listings and look for a sold action — only pause, resume and unavailable exist

title: The seller's new-Peek-Request notification deep-links to the buyer page and there is no top-level seller queue route
evidence: The alert inserted for the listing owner sets link '/peek-requests'. App.jsx:191 routes /peek-requests to BuyerPeekRequests, the buyer-side page. No route resolves to a seller fulfilment queue; the seller components are BuyerPeekRequestsQueue and ResponsePeekBindingQueue, reached from elsewhere.
impact: A seller notified of a buyer's Peek Request follows the link and may land on a page that does not show the request. This is the entry point of the product's core differentiating journey, so a dead-ending deep link here breaks the loop at its most fragile moment.
reproduction: Trigger a Peek Request against a listing you own on another account, then follow the notification link as the seller
root_cause: Notification link written before the seller queue had its own route
recommended_fix: Add a dedicated seller queue route and point the owner alert at it
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting the owner alert link resolves to a route that renders the seller fulfilment queue
notes: The underlying accept_peek_request authorization is correct; this is routing only

title: Messaging has no realtime transport and no refetch on focus or reconnect, so new messages can go unseen
evidence: @supabase/realtime-js is aliased to a stub that throws if .channel() is ever called, and Realtime is disabled in supabase/config.toml. query-client.js sets staleTime 30 minutes, gcTime 1 hour, refetchOnWindowFocus false and refetchOnReconnect false.
impact: A buyer or seller can sit on an open conversation and not see a reply until they navigate. In a market where WhatsApp is the competing channel and connectivity is intermittent, silent message latency pushes users off-platform, which also defeats the contact-privacy boundary the product works hard to maintain.
reproduction: Send a message from a second account and observe the first client without navigating
root_cause: Realtime deliberately removed for bundle size and cost; polling or focus-refetch was not substituted
recommended_fix: Enable refetchOnWindowFocus and refetchOnReconnect for conversation queries, or add interval polling on the active thread, or restore Realtime for messaging only
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting an inbound message appears within a bounded interval without manual navigation
notes: Stubbing Realtime is a defensible bundle decision; the gap is that nothing replaced it
